title: Honor selected connection and library ingredients

dependencies.stack: Owner-approved unmerged stack. F-07 is a compile dependency because this extends its real durable job service. No rebase of the parallel D or Q branches.

concurrency.overlap: Q-03 PR #753 also edits workflow-composer.ts and composition-provenance.ts. Public APIs remain additive; retain Q-03 planning policy and regenerate its prompt pins for w8-3-ingredients during integration. No cross-chat messages or branch changes.

activation.identity: Both registrations reference the actual configured composition provider. Provider/database readiness and existing panel authentication are required.

implementation: Strict typed connection and installed library-action identities, required flags, package versions and deterministic action contract revisions, separate from prose; durable job/journal preservation and replay conflict checks.

Paged safe discovery and metadata-only validation of availability, project/account ownership, auth compatibility and binding ambiguity. Connection values, private metadata and labels never enter composition prompts.
All candidate paths and repairs enforce required use; incompatible inputs and unresolved ingredient requirements return blockers without substitution or installation.

Revalidate in atomic draft attachment; immutable flow requirements survive restart and are enforced by readiness, enable, publish, live-draft edits and nested-workflow validation even with authoring disabled.
Derive installed package versions on extraction and cache hits without additional engine starts or cache rebuild. Advance prompt provenance; preserve F-07 recovery and legacy requests.

acceptance.check: Connections and similarly named library nodes cannot be confused; no secrets in prompts
acceptance.evidence: Same exact ID across both kinds, unreadable credential/private-label canaries, foreign owner/project and auth mismatch tests.

acceptance.check: Long/multiple selections survive repairs; invalid/incompatible nodes block instead of substitution
acceptance.evidence: 22 long selections survive bounded repair; one-shot, inline-to-fallback and submit_flow paths tested; missing IDs/actions, wrong accounts, stale package/action versions and explicit report_blocked covered.

Metadata changes during inference create no draft; later revocation/deletion/retarget/replacement and version drift block readiness/enable/publish. Metadata/graph edits cannot erase pins. Disk reopen retains requirements.

acceptance.check: No catalog rebuild or piece installation; additive contract and rollback
acceptance.evidence: Only existing catalog metadata and connection columns read. Cache tests prove versioned hits without new engines. F07 schema upgrade permits old inserts. Guide documents flag rollback and pre-F08 downgrade limits.

verification.guards: Normal commit hooks required; final results and exact pushed-head CI recorded in the PR description. No full-suite claim from affected tests.

limitations: Structural use and installed-contract availability, not proof of every natural-language constraint, branch execution or remote credential validity.
Current single-user/project identity is server-owned. Managed jarvis: credential sources without stable connection rows, unsupported external binding syntax and unversioned catalogs fail explicitly.
One installed version per piece; no historical package installation or parallel-version execution. Revalidation uses the current installed catalog and its normal refresh lifecycle.

Pinned requirements are immutable for the resulting flow. Changing selections requires a new composition request and key. Binary downgrade to pre-F08 code loses enforcement; keep these flows disabled before downgrade.
No D-16 UI, paid model calls, real credential use, live activation or deployment. F-09 is not started.
rollback: Disable ingredient authoring/presentation; preserve job selections, journals, pins and drafts. Keep current readiness enforcement. Leave F08 workflows disabled before a pre-F08 binary downgrade. No replay or user-record deletion.
